author: Scott & Susan Anderson
name: Chocolate Sauce
recipeInstructions: Dissolve sugar and cocoa on low heat. Add evaporated milk and butter. Cook on medium heat.
Bring to boil and boil for 1 minute, stirring constantly. For fudgy sauce, boil for 3 to 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and add vanilla. Scott says it's all in the wrist!

author: Ellie Martin
name: Buttermilk Syrup
recipeIngredient: * To make ¾ cup buttermilk if you don’t have it, fill almost ¾ with milk and add a tablespoon of lemon juice and stir, then let sit for one minute
recipeInstructions: In a medium saucepan, combine butter, sugar, and buttermilk and bring to a boil.
Once it’s at a complete boil, let it boil for one minute.
Take off heat and whisk in baking soda and vanilla.
It will foam up during the boiling, and especially when other ingredients are added.
Serve with your favorite pancakes or waffles. Best served warm.

author: Sue Egbert
name: Cole Slaw Dressing
recipeInstructions: Mix and add to shredded cabbage. Makes a lot, but stores well in refrigerator for a month.

name: Cafe Rio Dressing

author: Misha Jones
name: Misha’s Alfredo Sauce
recipeIngredient: 1 cup grated cheddar cheese OR ¾ cup grated Parmesan cheese
recipeInstructions: Saute garlic in butter until slightly Brown. Next, pour heavy cream into pan and stir.
Add salt and pepper being to a boil and turn off the heat. Add cheese and stir.
Taste and add more salt if desired. You can also add granulated garlic if you feel it needs it at the end.
For an even thicker sauce add one tbsp flour to the heavy cream.

author: Grandma Arnold
name: Texas Barbecue Sauce
recipeInstructions: Mix all ingredients together in a saucepan and let simmer, 2 hours. When it thickens, use over meat.

author: Tracy White
name: White Sauce
recipeInstructions: Mix butter and flour together. Add the rest and cook in a frypan, for about 3 minutes, until thickened.

author: Janie Arnold (Reba Egbert)
name: Beef Jerky
recipeIngredient: 1 beef flank steak or round steak well trimmed
recipeInstructions: Cut steak lengthwise with grain into long strips, not more than 1/4 inch thick. Toss with soy sauce.
Arrange beef strips in single layer on wire rack and place on baking sheet.
Sprinkle with lemon pepper and onion or garlic salt. Place second rack on top and flip over. Remove top rack.
Sprinkle again with seasonings. Bake in very slow oven at 175 to 200 for about 5 hours.

author: CAFÉ RIO
name: CREAMY TOMATILLO SALAD DRESSING (CAFÉ RIO)
recipeIngredient: 2 cups prepared Hidden Valley Buttermilk Ranch Dressing
1 small bunch cilantro, large stems removed (about ½ cup chopped cilantro)
1 tsp. green Tabasco sauce or 1 diced jalapeno pepper
recipeInstructions: Prepare ranch dressing according to directions on package and set aside.
Remove large cilantro stems, then wash leaves and spin dry or dry with paper towels.

Add cilantro to food processor fitted with the steel blade and pulse until finely chopped. (If you don’t have a food processor, I’d chop all ingredients well by hand and then blend dressing in a blender.)
Add tomatillos, garlic, lime juice, and green Tabasco or chopped jalapeno to the food processor and pulse until ingredients are finely pureed.
Add the 2 cups of prepared dressing and pulse just a few times, until ingredients are well combined.
Chill dressing for an hour or two and serve.

author: CAFÉ RIO
name: GREEN ENCHILADA SAUCE (CAFÉ RIO)
recipeIngredient: 1 ½ lbs. tomatillos, husked and quartered (4 medium to large equals ½ cup)
recipeInstructions: In large sauce pan or stock pot, heat olive oil over medium heat. Sauté onions and garlic until tender and fragrant.

While onions are sautéing, combine tomatillos, green peppers, jalapeno peppers, and cilantro in your blender. Process until smooth; you may have to do it in batches and add some chicken brother to make things blendable.
Pour the tomatillo mixture over the onions and garlic and add chicken broth, salt, pepper, and cumin.

Simmer 15 minutes-1 hour, depending on the consistency you want. I usuall turn the heat to high and boil it uncovered until I reach the consistency I want; it makes things go a lot faster. The sauce can also be simmered in a slow cooker all day.
Serve over tacos as an enchilada sauce, inside burritos and over burritos or as a dip for chips.

name: EASY BEEF MARINADE
recipeInstructions: Sprinkle meat with garlic powder, Lawry’s seasoning salt, pepper and soy sauce.
Put in covered container in refrigerator for at least 1 hour, longer is a little better. I use this on steaks and kabobs both.
